metadata.title: Your First Brutalist Project.
metadata.audience: Humanitarians AI fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Episode 3 of the Brutalist playlist. Teaches fellows who already have Claude Code how a first Brutalist project actually flows: tiny research question, evidence, ask Claude Code for an AI Explainer, watch it, request one visible revision, rebuild, verify — then face format discipline (native 16:9 and 9:16, not a crop) and submission lanes (GitHub source, Drive video). A runtime receipt is not publication approval. Outro variant is ClaudeTitleOutroHAI so the HAI handle is honored while the visual grammar stays claude-liam. Narration voice: Kokoro am_onyx (Liam).

skin_warnings: B11: palette=claude but the outro is 'ClaudeTitleOutroHAI' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — the Claude UI, the ask, the answer. Introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Your first Brutalist project starts here — one ask into Claude Code, and a plan comes back. Not a demo. A claim, with a script, a storyboard, and a clock.

shot.show: the Claude composer with the first-project ask and a four-line plan

props.command: claude "make me a 60-second Brutalist AI Explainer about how ribosomes read mRNA — 12 beats, Kokoro am_onyx, stop at the review cut"
output: renders scenes, compiles a review cut

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer lands the frame. Correction: demo -> claim. lead_silence_s written on the beat.
beats.narration_text: So here's the frame. Your first project is not a demo of a tool. It's a claim — a small research question, with evidence — that Claude Code renders into a one minute film you can rebuild, beat by beat. That is the whole method. Everything else is scaffolding.

shot.show: the hesitant writer typing 'Your first Brutalist project is a demo.' and correcting 'demo' -> 'claim'

props.text:
Your first Brutalist project
is a demo
Evidence in a one minute film
Written and rebuilt.

beats.role_note: framework beat — what a beat sheet IS. The file the whole reel conforms to.
beats.narration_text: The video is a file. beat_sheet dot json holds every beat, its narration line, its visual pattern, and its measured audio length. Everything downstream reads this. Change a line here — you re-render one beat, not a whole reel.

shot.show: a beat_sheet.json fragment — one beat as it lives on disk

props.title: beat_sheet.json
props.sparkLine: The video IS the file. One beat, one record.

beats.role_note: ASK-RESULT pair 1 — the concrete ask that starts a project. SPARK-LINE greeting.
beats.narration_text: So here is a first ask, verbatim. A specific topic, a length, the beat count, the voice, and a hard stop at the review cut so nothing final gets built before you have watched it.

shot.show: the Claude composer with a specific, paste-ready first-project ask

props.command: claude "in this folder, use skills/make/ai-explainer to make a 60-second AI Explainer on how ribosomes read mRNA. 12 beats, Kokoro am_onyx, review cut only."
output: stop at review-cut.mp4 for human review

beats.role_note: the seven things Claude Code actually touches on a first project — the mental model.
beats.narration_text: Claude Code does seven concrete things before you see a frame. It reads the skill, drafts the beat sheet, generates the audio, renders the scenes, compiles a review cut, writes the checks report, and stops. Every one leaves a file you can open.

shot.show: an artifact card listing the seven concrete steps Claude Code performs on a first project

artifactLines: reads skills/make/ai-explainer/SKILL.md
drafts beat_sheet.json (twelve beats)
generates mp3/beat-*.mp3 with Kokoro am_onyx
renders media/*.mp4 (one per Remotion beat)
compiles clips/ -> review-cut.mp4 at 4K
writes CHECKS-REPORT.md and _qc/ frames
stops for you to watch, before anything final

beats.role_note: the review cut is what you actually watch — a receipt from the compiler, not publication.
beats.narration_text: The output is a review cut. Twelve conformed clips, one narration per beat, four thousand pixels wide. That's the file you scrub. Not a Short. Not a published master. A local receipt that says: the pipeline finished — now you judge it.

shot.show: the review cut card — what compile.py leaves on disk for the fellow to watch

props.artifactHeading: The pipeline finished. Now you judge it.
artifactLines: twelve conformed per-beat clips in clips/
muxed to one review-cut.mp4 at 3840 x 2160
narration is the master clock — visuals conform
a per-beat manifest hashes each input for cache
not a Short, not a published master, a receipt
human review is a separate step — you watch it

beats.role_note: ASK-RESULT pair 2 — the revision loop. One beat changes, nothing else.
beats.narration_text: Something is off. Beat five drags. So you don't rebuild the film. You say what's wrong, and name the beat. Claude regenerates only that beat's audio, re-renders only that beat's scene, and re-muxes. Everything else is cached.

shot.show: the composer with the revision ask — one named beat, one instruction

props.command: claude "beat five is too long. cut the narration to twenty words, regenerate its audio, re-render its scene, and rebuild only the review cut."

beats.role_note: the effect of the revision — one clip changed on disk, nothing else. audio-first is the reason.
beats.narration_text: The diff on disk is small: one mp3 replaced, one mp4 replaced, one line in the beat sheet. That's why audio is the clock, and every beat is a slot. You change a beat by changing its slot — not by nudging a timeline.

shot.show: the tiny on-disk change that follows a one-beat revision

props.title: diff — after the one-beat revision
props.code:
M  beat_sheet.json          # narration_text on B05
M  mp3/beat-B05.mp3         # Kokoro am_onyx, re-measured
M  media/B05.mp4            # Remotion re-render
M  clips/B05.mp4            # compile.py re-conformed
M  review-cut.mp4           # concat+mux only

# 5 files changed. 11 clips cached.
# Audio is the clock; a beat is a slot.

beats.role_note: format discipline — 9:16 is a separate sheet, not a crop; art vertical plans.
beats.narration_text: Now the shape of the deliverable. Fellows owe two ratios per video, sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen. The vertical is not a crop of the landscape. It is its own beat sheet, in a sibling folder, with portrait-native scenes. The art vertical skill plans that sheet — you still author it.

shot.show: an artifact card that draws the sixteen-by-nine and nine-by-sixteen deliverables side by side

props.artifactHeading: 9:16 is a separate sheet, never a crop.
artifactLines: landscape master: 3840 x 2160, this beat_sheet.json
portrait companion: 2160 x 3840, vertical/beat_sheet.json
art vertical PLANS a portrait sheet — you still author it
each ratio uses portrait-native scenes (Composer916, Outro916)
compile.py renders each aspect at 4K natively
no cropping, no upscaling — layouts are ratio-aware
expect a real re-author, not a magic reframe

beats.role_note: no-source-no-verdict + honest limit: a runtime receipt is not publication approval.
beats.narration_text: And the handoff. Source goes to GitHub — the beat sheet, prompts, checks, README, anything under twenty-five megabytes. Video files go to Drive. A compile that finishes is a runtime receipt. It is not publication approval. That's the human review step, and it comes last.

shot.show: the two-lane handoff — source to GitHub, video to Drive; runtime receipt is not publication

props.artifactHeading: Source to GitHub. Video to Drive.
artifactLines: beat_sheet.json, README, PROMPTS.md -> GitHub branch + PR
MP4s and MP3s -> shared Google Drive folder
over-25-MB files always go to Drive, not the repo
no credentials or private data in either place
'compile finished' is a runtime receipt, nothing more
human review is a separate step — Bear watches it
publishing happens later — outside this pipeline

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — greeting Your Turn, paste-ready prompt Liam reads aloud, then a note on what a good answer looks like.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this prompt into Claude Code in a fresh folder, and swap in your topic. A good first ask names one small question, states the length in seconds, and stops at the review cut. A bad first ask says 'make me a video' and hopes.

shot.show: the composer with the viewer's paste-ready first-project prompt

props.command: claude "in this folder, use skills/make/ai-explainer to make a 60-second Brutalist AI Explainer about [my one tiny question]. 12 beats, Kokoro am_onyx, stop at the review cut so I can watch it before anything is submitted."
output: GOOD: one question, a length, a hard stop
BAD: 'make me a video' with no shape
watch the review cut — request ONE revision
